title: Reservoir Cursor + Slabbed Prefetch for Smoother Dashboard Pagination
creator: Priya Patel
description: Problem: Large dashboard queries (time-range exports, user cohorts, and long-scroll views) suffer from tail latency spikes and high read amplification when clients iterate pages quickly or jump to deep offsets. Current cursor pagination often issues broad range reads that cause hot I/O and CPU spikes for a small subset of tenants.
proposal: Introduce a lightweight in-memory 'reservoir cursor' layer combined with slabbed prefetch tiers on the shard coordinator. The reservoir cursor holds a bounded sampler of recent row keys for active scroll sessions and exposes a fast path for small-step pagination (next/prev). For larger jumps, the slabbed prefetcher materializes coarse page anchors (slabs) asynchronously and serves read-miss hedging to avoid blocking user requests.
design_notes: 1) Reservoir cursor structure: fixed-size ring per-session + eviction by session activity; stores (shard_id, row_key, last_seen_token). 2) Slabbed prefetch tiers: hot slab (in-RAM), warm slab (local SSD cache), cold slab (remote store snapshot). 3) Hedging policy: when a query path misses reservoir, issue speculative read to warm slab and simultaneously to cold store if latency > threshold. 4) Backpressure: throttle slab materialization to configured bytes/sec and apply per-tenant fairness tokens. 5) Consistency: reservoir entries are advisory—on mismatch we fall back to canonical index scan with monotonic anchor to avoid duplication or gaps.
tradeoffs: Pros: reduces small-step tail latency, lowers read amplification for hot cursors, provides graceful degradation when slab tiers are unavailable. Cons: additional memory per active session, complexity in eviction/TTL tuning, potential for stale anchors requiring validation. We accept occasional extra reads for correctness under worst-case churn.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 95th percentile paginated-next latency reduced by >=30% for top-10 tenants in load tests. 2) End-to-end read amplification (IO bytes/read) reduced by >=20% under representative workloads. 3) No correctness regressions for pagination (no duplicates/missing rows) in 1000 randomized replay tests. 4) Feature gated behind runtime flag and can be rolled back without data migration.
metrics_and_monitoring: Track metrics: reservoir_hit_rate, slab_prefetch_latency_ms{tier}, slab_materialization_bytes, per_tenant_prefetch_tokens, pagination_95th_ms, pagination_99th_ms, read_amplification_ratio. Create a dashboard and set alerts: slab_prefetch_latency_ms > 500ms (P1), reservoir_hit_rate < 0.6 for top-20 sessions (P2).
rollout_plan: 1) Unit + integration tests. 2) Canary deploy to internal namespace with synthetic workloads and compare against control for 72h. 3) Gradual rollout to 10% of prod tenants by runtime flag. 4) Observe metrics for 7 days; if regressions, roll back and run deeper profiling.
safety_and_mitigation: Circuit-breaker on reservoir memory; if memory pressure detected, drain least-active sessions. Slab materialization capped and queue length monitored. Operations runbook added for rollback and for purging slab caches.
benchmarks: Local perf harness (60k item list, 50 concurrent scroll sessions): baseline 95th=420ms, with reservoir+slabbed prefetch 95th=280ms (33% improvement). Read amplification baseline=4.2x, after change=3.1x (26% improvement). Results with hedging enabled show higher tail for cold reads but reduced user-visible latency.
